extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary and K-12 recipients (college/university and school administrators), Title IX Coordinators, institutional policymakers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how educational institutions must respond to sexual harassment under Title IX, including mandatory elements of grievance processes, duties triggered by actual knowledge, supportive measures, due process protections, and documentation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible employees / mandatory reporters designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may designate which employees are mandatory reporters (employees who must report sexual harassment to the Title IX Coordinator), which employees may listen to disclosures without being required to report, and/or which employees must report only with the complainant's consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department leaves recipients wide discretion to craft employee reporting policies; regardless of designation, students and employees must be notified of the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and have clear reporting channels, including options accessible even during non-business hours. The mere ability or obligation to report or having received training does not by itself make someone an 'official with authority.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure channels and notice for reporting (actual knowledge trigger)
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the actual knowledge condition, the Department intends every complainant to know that if or when the complainant desires the recipient to respond, the complainant has clear, accessible channels by which to report and/or file a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide accessible reporting mechanisms (including non-business hours) and notify students and employees of the Title IX Coordinator contact information so that a complaint can trigger the recipient's response obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect complainant autonomy and control
rubrics_metrics.description: Respecting an alleged victim's autonomy, giving alleged victims control over how official systems respond, and offering clear options are critical aspects of helping an alleged victim recover from sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department aims to respect complainant autonomy and recognizes the importance of complainants retaining as much control as possible, while ensuring clear information about supportive measures and how to file a formal complaint if the complainant desires institutional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate indifference standard (adapted)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient acts with deliberate indifference when it responds to sexual harassment in a manner that is 'clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.' The Department adopts, but adapts, the Gebser/Davis deliberate indifference standard for administrative enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations impose a general obligation not to act clearly unreasonably and add specific mandatory obligations on recipients so the Department can hold recipients accountable for responding meaningfully upon actual knowledge of sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness of response
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's response must be prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptness is a required element of the response specified in §106.44(a); failure to respond promptly may be evidence of deliberate indifference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures to complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's response must consist of offering supportive measures to a complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be offered regardless of whether the complainant files or the Title IX Coordinator signs a formal complaint, and must be tailored to each complainant's unique circumstances. They must be offered not only during an investigation but regardless of whether any investigation is pending or occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator outreach about supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must ensure the Title IX Coordinator contacts each complainant to discuss supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes regarding supportive measures, inform the complainant of availability of supportive measures with or without filing, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mandatory, proactive, and interactive process helps ensure complainants receive the response that will most effectively address their needs in each circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's response must treat complainants and respondents equitably: offer supportive measures to complainants and follow a grievance process that complies with §106.45 before imposing disciplinary sanctions on respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a respondent is found responsible, the recipient must effectively implement remedies for the complainant designed to restore or preserve equal educational access, and may impose disciplinary sanctions on the respondent only after a compliant grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must not be punitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures cannot be punitive or disciplinary against any party and cannot unreasonably burden the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations clarify that supportive measures are distinct from punitive interim actions or disciplinary sanctions and should not function as punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary sanctions require §106.45-compliant grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary sanctions cannot be imposed on a respondent without following a grievance process that complies with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations require fair investigation and adjudication before imposing disciplinary sanctions; interim or punitive actions that bypass the grievance process are not authorized as sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator as sole official authorized to initiate grievance
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Title IX Coordinator is authorized to initiate a grievance process against a respondent by signing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction is intended to ensure that initiation of formal grievance processes against a complainant's wishes is undertaken only by a trained official and only when circumstances justify overriding the complainant's preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of non-investigation decisions under deliberate indifference
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's decision not to investigate when the complainant does not wish to file will be evaluated under the deliberate indifference standard—i.e., whether that decision was clearly unreasonable in light of the known circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, a Title IX Coordinator's decision to sign a formal complaint initiating a grievance against a complainant's wishes will be considered under the deliberate indifference standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal authority with procedural safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent from education programs or activities on an emergency basis, with or without a grievance process pending, provided post-deprivation notice and opportunity to challenge the removal are given to the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient's decision to initiate an emergency removal will be evaluated under the deliberate indifference standard; emergency removals must be accompanied by notice and an opportunity to challenge after the fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of reasons for responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must document their reasons why each response to sexual harassment was not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting the justification for responses provides evidence a recipient met its obligations under the final regulations and facilitates Department enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not restrict constitutional rights to satisfy Title IX duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department may not require a recipient to restrict rights protected under the U.S. Constitution (First, Fifth, Fourteenth Amendments) to satisfy the duty not to be deliberately indifferent under the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not view restrictions of constitutional rights as a means of satisfying Title IX obligations; enforcement must be consistent with constitutional guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be adequate, reliable, and impartial
rubrics_metrics.description: Equitable grievance procedures should provide an adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation of complaints, including the opportunity to present witnesses and other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should be prompt, thorough, and impartial; specific steps vary with case nature, complainant source, age of students, institutional size and structure, and other factors, but the inquiry must always be prompt, thorough, and impartial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process core requirements (notice and meaningful opportunity to be heard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural due process requires at a minimum notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard; due process is flexible and calls for procedural protections as the particular situation demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations prescribe a grievance process grounded in due process principles to benefit both complainants and respondents, providing specific procedures reasonably designed for implementation in educational settings rather than adopting court or administrative adjudicatory rules wholesale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural fairness enhances legitimacy and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fair process or procedural justice increases outcome legitimacy and compliance because it is likely to lead to an accurate outcome and conveys respect and value to individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The §106.45 grievance process seeks a fair, truth-seeking process that improves the perception and reality that determinations represent just outcomes, reducing bias and increasing the accuracy and legitimacy of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process tailored to educational context
rubrics_metrics.description: The standardized Title IX sexual harassment grievance process contains procedural requirements, rights, and protections reasonably designed for implementation in the setting of an education program or activity, recognizing schools are not courts and lack subpoena powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process protections in Title IX contexts may differ from criminal or administrative contexts and may vary between elementary/secondary and postsecondary institutions; the regulations aim to balance accuracy, fairness, and practicability in educational settings.
